case.description: TEST-ONLY: a countersink near a bend, and one with no flat to measure.

findings.message: These countersinks are clear of the public value, so nothing is known about them: only a shop's own number can say a countersink is fine.
needs: The shop's own number for a countersink's depth.

requirement.source: PCBWay, countersink and counterbore design guidelines: at most 0.70t. Fictiv's 60 to 70% agrees at its top end: https://www.pcbway.com/blog/Sheet_Metal/Countersink_Counterbore_Holes_Design_Guidelines_f328f60a.html
requirement.text: At most 1.05 mm. The countersink's depth, from the skin to where the cone meets the hole's wall.

location.text: the countersink of hole 1, at x 8.5, y 12.5, z 0.75

findings.message: The countersink of hole 1: its rim's distance to a cut edge, on this flat's outline, is 3 mm, below a public value of 4 mm. A person decides.
needs: The shop's own number for a countersink's distance to a cut edge.

requirement.source: Geomiq, sheet metal design guide: 4t from an edge to the countersink's centre, moved to the rim by taking off half the major diameter d. Xometry also gives 4t: https://geomiq.com/sheet-metal-design-guide/
requirement.text: At least 4 mm. The countersink's rim to the nearest cut edge on the same flat. Another countersink's rim counts as a cut edge.

findings.message: These countersinks are clear of the public value, so nothing is known about them: only a shop's own number can say a countersink is fine.

requirement.text: At least 5 mm. The countersink's rim to the nearest cut edge on the same flat. Another countersink's rim counts as a cut edge.

location.text: the countersink of hole 1, at x 8.5, y 12.5, z 0.75

findings.message: The countersink of hole 1: its rim's distance to bend 1 is 2 mm, below a public value of 2.5 mm. A person decides.
needs: The shop's own number for a countersink's distance to a bend.

requirement.source: Geomiq, sheet metal design guide: 3t from the bend line to the countersink's centre, moved to the rim. Its bend line is read as the bend's tangent, an assumption. Xometry also gives 3t: https://geomiq.com/sheet-metal-design-guide/
requirement.text: At least 2.5 mm. The countersink's rim to the nearest bend tangent on the same flat.

findings.message: A hole here isn't on a flat that ends at a bend, so its distance to a bend wasn't measured.
needs: A person to look at those faces, because this version can't check them.

bends_gate.message: 1 bend found. Every face has a label, and skins that aren't in one plane join only through bends. This only says the bends were found.

exceptions: A punching figure used as a floor for every process, so it can only warn.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.
requirements.rights: Unclear. One published figure, restated with its source and not copied text. The publisher's terms have not been checked.
requirements.source: Mate Precision Technologies, punching: 0.5t, its lowest figure, for fully guided tooling in aluminium. Used for every process and material, so it assumes nothing about this part: https://www.mate.com/technical-resources/punch-press-resources/tips-techniques/punching/techniques/holes/

exceptions: Published values differ by more than six times, and the source doesn't say which process it means.
requirements.measuring_line: The hole's edge to the nearest cut edge on the same flat.
requirements.method: The most lenient published value we may use. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.

exceptions: Worded as a risk: the file can't say whether a hole is cut after bending.
requirements.measuring_line: 2.5t + r, a labelled trial value: the hole's edge to the nearest bend tangent on the same flat.
requirements.method: A labelled trial value. Below it a person looks; above it nothing is known.

requirements.source: PTC Creo design rules default, also in Five Flute and Fictiv, which probably share one origin: https://support.ptc.com/help/creo/creo_pma/r7.0/usascii/sheetmetal/sheetmetaldesign/Set_Up/About_Design_Rules.html

exceptions: Geomiq's depth figure, 0.6 mm below the material thickness, was read again on 2026-11-10 and is still unclear in what it measures, so it isn't used.

exceptions: PCBWay's centre to edge of twice the major diameter is stricter whenever d is more than 2t.

exceptions: If Geomiq's bend line is the bend's centreline, the published value is lower than this by half the bend allowance, which r and t can't write exactly.

exceptions: Mate also gives 2t. A lower laser figure from one shop's own specification is left out.

thickness_gate.message: The model's sheet matches the declared 1.5 mm within 0.02 mm, a placeholder. This only says it matches what was declared. It doesn't confirm that value is the real gauge.
